title: bgtracker hero tips
description: Community-written strategy tips shown under each hero in the draft. One entry per Battlegrounds hero cardId. Every tip must be ORIGINAL text or contributed under the repository licence - never copied, paraphrased or machine-reworded from anyone else's guide. tests/test_regression.py enforces this file's shape offline, so a pull request that breaks it fails CI. This file is what SHIPS, and what the overlay falls back to whenever anything else is missing. There is a second, voted route: server/tips.py takes submissions and votes and publishes hero-tips-community.json, whose entries obey the same 'when' and 'bullets' rules stated here; a hero appears in that file only once the vote cleared its floors, and the overlay marks such a line so it is never mistaken for a reviewed one.

version.description: Schema version of this file. Bump only when the shape changes.

schema.description: Filename of this schema, for editors that follow it.

note.description: Free text for human editors. Ignored by the app.

tips.description: Battlegrounds hero cardId -> one tip. The cardId is the id HearthstoneJSON gives the hero (bgtracker.bg_ids()['heroes']), e.g. 'BG26_HERO_101'. An unknown cardId fails the test rather than silently doing nothing.

name.description: The hero's name. Informational only - the app looks the hero up by cardId. Spell it the way the card database spells it so the file stays greppable.

when.description: ONE line: when this hero is good. This is the line the overlay prints under the hero during the draft, so it must stand alone and stay short - past about 50 characters it is truncated on screen. No trailing full stop.

bullets.description: One to three short notes: how to play it, what it needs, what it costs. Not drawn in the draft window today - they are the reference half of the entry and the place to put detail.

tribes.description: Optional: the tribes this hero's own power names or needs. Uppercase, exactly as Hearthstone spells them. Leave it out unless the printed power really is tribe-locked.
